item.text: The implementation now writes native maps on all event ingestion paths, reads both map and legacy formats, and converts old rows under a shared distributed lock. The migration stores its DynamoDB scan key after each completed batch page, so interrupted pages can be safely rescanned without duplicating or losing records. I’m reviewing the diff and edge cases before the final verification run.

func TestEventFieldsMapEncodingAndLegacyReading(t *testing.T) {
	legacyJSON := []byte(`{"user":"alice","count":9007199254740993,"nested":{"enabled":true},"emptyObject":{},"emptyList":[],"values":[1,2.5]}`)
	fieldsMap, err := encodeFieldsMap(legacyJSON)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	item, err := dynamodbattribute.MarshalMap(map[string]interface{}{keyFieldsMap: fieldsMap})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, item[keyFieldsMap].M)
	require.NotNil(t, item[keyFieldsMap].M["emptyObject"].M)
	require.NotNil(t, item[keyFieldsMap].M["emptyList"].L)

	e, err := unmarshalEvent(item)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	got, _, err := decodeEventFields(e)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	var want events.EventFields
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(legacyJSON, &want))
	require.Equal(t, want, got)

	legacyEvent := event{Fields: string(legacyJSON)}
	legacyFields, _, err := decodeEventFields(legacyEvent)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, want, legacyFields)
}

item.text:
Implemented native DynamoDB `FieldsMap` storage across all event write paths, with readers that accept both `FieldsMap` and legacy `Fields` data.

Added an automatically started migration that uses batch writes, validates converted metadata, records resumable checkpoints under `backend.FlagKey`, logs problematic records, and shares the existing distributed migration lock.

Added focused tests for map conversion, legacy reads, empty collections, and flag key composition.

Verification passed: `go test ./lib/events/dynamoevents ./lib/backend`; `git diff --check` is clean.
